problem: At a geological site, an object is found with $95%$ of its original lutetium-176 content. Given that the half-life of lutetium-176 is $37.64$ billion years, approximately how old is the object?
worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=37.64$ billion years, we have

$$
37.64=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{37.64}.
$$

So, we have

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64}.
$$

We wish to calculate the time $t$ such that $M(t)=0.95{M}_{0}.$ So, we set up our equation as follows:

$$
0.95{M}_{0}={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64}
$$

Solving this equation for $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.95{M}_{0} & ={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64} \\ 0.95\cancel{{M}_{0}} & =\cancel{{M}_{0}}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64} \\ 0.95 & ={e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.95) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/37.64}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.95) & =-\frac{t\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{37.64} \\ t & =-\frac{37.64\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.95)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ t & ≈2.785\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the object is approximately $2.785$ billion years old.
